title: Deep learning image reconstruction generates thinner slice iodine maps with improved image quality to increase diagnostic acceptance and lesion conspicuity: a prospective study on abdominal dual-energ
summary: Prospective comparison in 104 participants/136 lesions found deep-learning reconstruction at 1.25-mm thickness reduced iodine-map noise and improved radiologist diagnostic acceptability/lesion conspicuity versus iterative reconstruction, while measured iodine concentrations were unchanged.
ai_technology: DLIR reconstructs thin-slice iodine maps from dual-energy CT data.

evidence.tested: Prospective comparison in 104 participants/136 lesions found deep-learning reconstruction at 1.25-mm thickness reduced iodine-map noise and improved radiologist diagnostic acceptability/lesion conspicuity versus iterative reconstruction, while measured iodine concentrations were unchanged.
evidence.unknown: The result is limited to the reported dataset, experimental setting and validation in this study; broader generalization and real-world benefit are not established.
